h: Dangote Refinery considers bigger IPO after ₦6 trillion in subscriptions
p: Dangote Petroleum Refinery is reportedly considering enlarging its share sale by up to 30% after investors put in nearly ₦6 trillion. That could take the offer to about $2.1 billion, one of Africa's largest.
body: Dangote Petroleum Refinery is reportedly considering expanding its initial public offering (IPO) by as much as 30%, after strong investor demand pushed subscriptions to nearly ₦6 trillion, or about $4.5 billion.

The refinery, owned by billionaire Aliko Dangote, initially planned to sell 4.1 billion shares. Demand is said to have exceeded the shares on offer by nearly three times, prompting talks about increasing the allocation.
If the expansion goes ahead, the value of the share sale could rise to about $2.1 billion, potentially making it one of the biggest stock market offerings on the continent.
The refinery is the largest in Africa, and its pricing decisions have recently driven changes in pump prices across Nigeria.

Aliko Dangote is now reportedly considering selling part of his personal stake in the refinery after applications worth about ₦5.85 trillion, or $4.3 billion, exceeded the company's target of $1.6 billion to $2.1 billion. He is said to have opened talks with the Securities and Exchange Commission on the move, which would give more investors a chance to own shares.
more: The offer could grow to about $2.1 billion.
Demand was nearly three times the shares on offer.
